adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — No start barrier ensures the reader performs even one request before deletion finishes, so fast deletion can let the concurrency test pass without exercising concurrent access.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test design issue in the new test method. Looking at the diff, the test creates groups, starts a reader thread, then immediately begins deleting groups. There's no synchronization mechanism (like a CountDownLatch or barrier) to ensure the reader thread has actually started and performed at least one read before deletions begin. If the main thread deletes all groups very quickly, the reader thread might never execute a concurrent read during deletion, making the test ineffective at catching race conditions. This is a legitimate test quality concern for newly added test code, not a bug in production code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:152 — If any deletion throws before deletedAll is set, the non-daemon reader loops forever and can leak into later tests or prevent the test JVM from exiting.

adjudication.rationale: The test code shows that the reader thread runs in a while loop checking `!deletedAll.get()`. The deletion loop at lines 155-157 iterates through groupUuuids and calls remove() on each. If any deletion throws an exception, the code would exit before reaching `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 158, leaving the reader thread running indefinitely. The thread is not a daemon thread (created with `new Thread()`), so it would prevent JVM exit and could leak into subsequent tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:155 — The test signals the reader to stop but never joins it, so the assertion can run before a concurrent request records its exception and falsely pass the regression.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while !deletedAll.get(), catching exceptions into caughtExceptions. After deleting groups, it sets deletedAll.set(true) and immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty. However, there's no Thread.join() or synchronization to ensure the reader thread has finished its current iteration before the assertion runs. The reader thread could be mid-request when deletedAll becomes true, and if that request fails, the exception would be added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed. This is a real race condition that could cause the test to falsely pass.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:157 — The assertion runs without joining the reader thread, so an exception recorded after this check is missed and the regression test can falsely pass.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that collects exceptions into caughtExceptions while the main thread deletes groups. After deletion completes, deletedAll.set(true) is called and then assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) runs immediately. However, there's no Thread.join() or synchronization to ensure the reader thread has actually stopped and finished its last iteration. The reader thread could still be executing or about to add an exception after the assertion runs, causing the test to falsely pass. This is a real race condition bug in the test code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The reader is not coordinated to complete even one request during deletion, so the test can pass without exercising the concurrent nullable-model path it is meant to cover.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a test design issue. The test creates a reader thread that loops while deletedAll is false, but there's no synchronization to ensure the reader thread actually executes any requests before all deletions complete. The main thread could delete all groups and set deletedAll=true before the reader thread even starts its first iteration. This is a valid concern about test coverage - the test is meant to verify the concurrent nullable-model path (the fix in GroupAdapter.java where model can be null), but the test design doesn't guarantee this race condition is actually exercised. This is a real, specific issue with the new test code in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:139 — The non-daemon reader is stopped only on the normal deletion path, so any deletion failure leaves it spinning indefinitely and can hang the test process.

adjudication.rationale: The test creates a reader thread that loops while `!deletedAll.get()`. If any deletion in the `groupUuuids.forEach` block throws an exception, the code would exit before reaching `deletedAll.set(true)`, leaving the reader thread spinning indefinitely. The thread is not set as daemon, so it would prevent the JVM/test process from terminating. This is a real defect in the test code introduced by this diff.
